title: Queueing systems
subtitle: Waiting is what most systems are made of. A few formulas tell you when the line explodes.

elems.title: Elements of a queue
elems.body: A queueing system has an arrival process (calling population, inter-arrival times), a queue (capacity, discipline — FIFO, LIFO, priority) and one or more servers (service-time distribution). Kendall’s notation A/B/c/K/N/D describes it: M/M/1 = Markovian (Poisson) arrivals, Markovian (exponential) service, one server. Applications: banks, call centres, routers, CPUs, traffic.

mm1.title: M/M/1 in theory
mm1.body: With arrival rate λ and service rate μ the utilisation is ρ = λ/μ, which must stay below 1. Then L (mean number in system) = ρ/(1−ρ), W (mean time in system) = 1/(μ−λ), Lq = ρ²/(1−ρ), Wq = ρ/(μ−λ), and Little’s law L = λW holds for any stable queue. At ρ = 0.5: L = 1. At ρ = 0.9: L = 9 — waiting explodes as utilisation approaches 100%.
mm1.steps: λ = 0.8 customers/min, μ = 1 customer/min. Mean number in system. Mean time in system, and Little’s law check L = λW.

sim.title: Simulating it
sim.body: Generate exponential inter-arrival and service times, run the event loop, and measure. With λ = 0.5, μ = 1 (ρ = 0.5) over 4000 customers the simulated utilisation is 0.512 and average number in system 1.012 against theory ρ = 0.5, L = 1. At ρ = 0.9 the theory says L = 9 and the simulation gives about 11.148 — with much more noise.

net.title: Networks of queues
net.body: Real systems chain queues: a customer visits several stations. In a tandem of M/M/1 queues, each behaves (Jackson's theorem) as an independent M/M/1 with the same arrival rate but its own μ, and the total time is the sum. More servers (M/M/c) share the load: the same λ with two half-speed servers behaves differently from one full-speed server.
net.steps: Two M/M/1 stations in series, λ = 2/min, μ₁ = 4, μ₂ = 3. W₁ = 1/(4−2) = 0.5 min, W₂ = 1/(3−2) = 1 min.

app.title: Applications
app.body: Sizing a call-centre (how many agents keep waiting under 30 s), router buffers, CPU scheduling, hospital beds, checkout lanes. The simulator shows the danger zone: keep utilisation below about 70–80% if waiting matters.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• ρ = λ/μ < 1; L = ρ/(1−ρ); W = 1/(μ−λ); L = λW.
  • Simulation agrees with theory, with noise growing near ρ = 1.
